input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) is the only termination-for-convenience mechanic in the Agreement. It gives AP an acceptable fallback-level exit (90 days' written notice for any reason after the one-year Initial Term, and the Initial Term itself is not longer than 12 months), and the only termination-related payment is fees generated during the 90-day termination period, i.e. no more than three months' fees. It fails the fallback on one material term: the right is mutual and untethered, so Kubient may walk away for convenience mid-term during any renewal term. An auto-renewal/notice mechanic is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term, so this is Vendor mid-term convenience termination rather than mere non-renewal. Our edit is the shortest conforming change: it preserves AP's 90-day right verbatim and confines Kubient's convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term, keeping its 90 days' notice. We have not pursued the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees), which is a poor fit for this revenue-share model with no prepaid fees.

proposal.summary: Limit Kubient's for-convenience termination to the end of the then-current Term while preserving AP's 90-day exit right.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have split the mutual post-Initial Term exit so that AP retains its right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time, while Kubient's convenience termination may only take effect at the end of the then-current Term. This is our fallback position; Kubient's 90 days' notice requirement is unchanged.
